page1.text:
"Damn... It..."
I try to fight back, but my body won't move.
My limbs aren't responding, my senses are being taken away, and I'm sure she's going to off me.

page2.text:
"Goodbye, boy. Regret that you became a Master with such little talent as you have."
My body doesn't move at all and accepts the finger tip of death.

page3.text:
"Nnng...!"
I resist the urge to close my eyes and keep glaring at Caster with all my might.

page4.text:
"Wow. Good boy, I can't say I dislike that in a person."
Caster snickers at my utmost resistance and puts her fingers on my Command Spells.

page5.text:
"Oh..."
...Even my free will is going numb.
...In my fading thoughts...
I...
...I hear the sound of clashing swords from the temple gate behind me.

page6.text:
!
What kind of miracle is this?
I hear the sound of dozens of objects splitting the air, followed by numerous arrows piercing the ground in front of me.
Caster instantly retreats, her black robe swirling like a spinning top.

page7.text:
"Wha—"
There are arrows piercing the ground by her feet.
Thirteen of them fired from the direction of the temple gate.
They were probably fired in rapid succession, and Caster would've been struck center mass had there been one more in the volley.

page8.text:
The one who fired stands there, atop the gate.
The knight in red then jumps down to ground level, his hands empty.

page9.text:
"Heh. I thought you'd be dead by now, but you're more persistent than I thought."
Archer moves to stand before me, as if to protect me.

page10.text:
"You... Why...?"
"What? I just happened to be in the area. Don't worry about it.
...So, how's your body? That should've cut Caster's string."

page11.text:
"Huh..."
I check my hand.
...It moves.
My frozen limbs must've regained mobility from that earlier action.

page12.text:
"I can move. Caster's spell is gone, but..."
"That's good. I want to tell you to do what you want now, but... If you don't want to get killed, then stay there for a while. One wrong move..."

page13.text:
"Khh, Archer...!? Ugh, what is Assassin doing...!"
"See, she'll take her anger out on you.
Hell hath no fury, as they say. What a pain in the ass this is gonna be."
Archer laughs. I can't tell how serious he is.

page14.text:
"...Well. Don't get too mad, Caster.
Assassin is fighting Saber. I don't know who that samurai is, but he is quite a swordsman to be able to hold Saber back.
Shouldn't you be praising him instead?"

page15.text:
Even though he's facing an enemy, there's no tension in his voice or body language at all.
Caster must've noticed that, and regains her composure.

page16.text: "...Hmph, don't be ridiculous. You cannot call him a Heroic Spirit if he can't even stop you. That man lacks ability despite calling himself a swordsman."

page17.text:
"Oh. You sound as if Assassin is your ally... So your Masters are cooperating after all.
If not, then it wouldn't explain this situation of two Servants in the same place."

page18.text:
Caster stares at Archer silently.
I can't see her expression well beneath her hood, but she looks as if she's agitated.

page19.text: "...Archer, is that true...!? Assassin and Caster's Masters are cooperating...!?"

page20.text:
"Yeah. Assassin is guarding the outside of the gate, and Caster is hiding inside. It's pretty obvious that these two have made a truce.
It is not rare for Masters to be cooperating with each other. You and Rin are cooperating, remember?"

page21.text:
"Oh."
That's right.
Then, there are two Masters at this Ryudou Temple...!?

page22.text:
"Heh...
Hehe...hahaha! I was wondering what you were going to say, but you are so off, Archer!"

page23.text: "Hm? Oh, I'm wrong? ...Man, I was confident that you two were allies."

page24.text:
"Yes, you are terribly wrong.
Allies, you said...? Me cooperating with that dog? With the man under my control?"

page25.text: Her laugh is so out of place that the tense atmosphere disperses.

page27.text:
"..."
Something finally comes out.
It's not Caster's enmity nor the swirl of magical energy surrounding the temple.
For the first time since he came here...
Archer is showing open hostility.

page28.text:
"Yes, your hunch is correct, Archer.
My Master is not cooperating with anyone, nor is Assassin's Master.
No, first of all, Assassin does not have a Master!"

page29.text:
"The...hell?"
Assassin doesn't have a Master...?
What does that mean?
Servants cannot exist without a Master.
Weren't they supposed to disappear if they don't have a supply of magical energy...?

page31.text:
"Of course not. I have not broken any rules. Mages summon Servants, right?
Then, what is the problem with a Caster, a mage, summoning a Servant!?"

page32.text:
The witch in black robes proclaims with a sneer.
...
...So that means...
The Assassin-class Servant at the temple gate is a Heroic Spirit summoned by Caster...!

page33.text:
"...A Servant controlling a Servant, huh... I see, so he's a fictitious Heroic Spirit.
As Assassin was not summoned by a proper Master, something other than a proper assassin must've been called. Eh, not that I care. Whatever the origins of the spirit, the job remains the same.
Though I would hazard to say you made this choice unilaterally, eh?"

page34.text: "...Fine, I'll ask. How did you come to that conclusion, Archer?"

page35.text:
"Oh, it's just a hunch. Masters are mages.
When a mage summons a spellcaster that is superior to them...I imagine their relationship isn't a normal Master-Servant one.
The Master-mage would always be on guard against the superior Caster-mage that they summoned.
...If I were your Master, I wouldn't be inclined to let a witch freely move about. There is no way that they'd allow you to summon another Servant that follows your orders, rather than theirs."

page36.text:
"...Heh. It seems you have some intelligence.
I will overlook your insult in lieu of your cleverness."

page37.text:
Caster snickers, though she watches Archer carefully.
...The only thing between them is enmity.
They're about seven meters apart.
With the charge that Archer showed at school, he should be able to slash Caster before she even finishes chanting an incantation.

page38.text:
"I understand now. Saber, Lancer, and Rider have strong Magic Resistance. The guy behind me doesn't even compare; it's on another level.
You'd have a hard time affecting them with magecraft. So you can't compete since you're stuck with spellwork."

page39.text:
"In that case, it's natural for you to resort to underhanded tactics.
You broke the rules to summon an Assassin-class Servant yourself...
Created territory here and collected souls from the people in town...
And you don't fight yourself, instead opting to watch the war's movements from afar.
Going so far, I assume that you have your Master basically tied up somewhere. Stuck a puppet like this dipshit Master behind me."

page40.text:
She smiles silently.
That sends a chill up my spine.
She's not only collecting magical energy from the people in town.
She's even using her own Master as her own tool just like she did to me...

page41.text:
...
...Caster is dangerous.
She's not a pure threat like Berserker, but those who make the situation worse without showing themselves are always the most problematic in a war.

page42.text:
"Yes. You are correct, Archer.
But you are wrong if you believe that I am no match for you people.
It is easy for me to win the Holy Grail War.
I am working hard as I am thinking ahead. I am not working out a strategy out of fear of you people."

page43.text: "...Oh? Did you say that it's easy to defeat us, Caster? Pretty words for a witch that flees all the time."

page44.text: "You heard me. If it's here, I am stronger than anyone else. Berserker and Saber aside, you won't be able to even scratch me."

page45.text:
"You should be the one who considers fleeing.
I forgave you once. But there won't be a second time.
I will dole out the appropriate punishment to those who call me a witch."

page46.text:
Caster's robe distorts.
The magical energy in the air becomes a dense fog covering Caster's body.
With that in front of him...
"...Interesting. Not even a scratch, you said?"
Though he's barely audible, Archer sounds amused.

page47.text:
"Yes. You will not even be able to touch me."
The black shadow responds.
The knight in red laughs.

page48.text:
"Then I'll take a shot. If I fail, I'll leave the rest to Saber."
He flies like a squall towards the black shadow.

page49.text:
The red shadow runs.
I don't know when he got them, but in Archer's hands are those weapons...twin swords.

page50.text:
"Oh...!"
He does not allow any time for chanting incantations.
Archer closes in on Caster before she can extend her arm.
He slashes her in half with those twin blades.

page51.text:
The robe, cut in half, scatters in the wind.
"Hm..."
Archer seems disappointed, standing in front of the remains of the enemy he just defeated so easily.

page52.text:
It looked disappointing.
She talked so big, yet she lost without even attacking him once.
Anyone would feel let down.

page53.text:
"..."
Archer is still gripping the twin swords.
"..."
A red knight.
The black and white short swords are magnificent to behold.
...Strange.
My eye really keeps getting drawn to them.

page54.text:
...Those twin swords.
They must be great swords with history, but I don't feel any malice from them.
Noble Phantasms are supposed to be fantastic weapons, so it only makes sense that they're beautifully crafted.
If Saber's sword was visible, I have to imagine it'd likewise be majestic.

page55.text:
These swords, however, are different.
A sword with the clear purpose of defeating opponents.
A sword that was made to leave a mark on history.
A sword forged to surpass the skill and craft of another.
A sword intended to do some great deed.
These blades have none of that. They're nothing like a blade with a famed story or magical lineage.

page56.text:
If anything, it seemed like they were made because someone just...wanted to.
There's something raw about them, unalloyed even. Made like their creator questioned their own significance.
That's what I think those are.
Mirrored swords without vanity.
Black and white. A swordsmith's awkward representation of yin and yang.

page57.text:
I stand captivated.
Because...I feel like the way they are is beautiful.

page58.text:
Caster's slashed body disappears.
...
After seeing it off, the moment Archer looks like he's going to put his weapons away—

page59.text: "I'm disappointed, Archer. You really are weak."

page60.text: Caster's voice echoes throughout the desolate temple.

page61.text:
"Guh...!"
Archer leaps.
The barrage from earlier is mirrored.
Bullets of light come flying from the sky to pierce Archer,
and Archer repels them with his twin swords.
No...
This is different from before.

page62.text:
"Wha—"
The ground is burnt red.
The magical energy compressed within one of those lights is at least three times greater than my full capacity.
I'm sure even Archer would have half his body blown away if he took a direct hit. He'd be just like Caster earlier.

page63.text:
I look up at the sky.
The moon isn't visible, veiled behind a sea of dark clouds.
In the middle of that, the black mage floats as if she reigns over the heavens.

page64.text:
"...It must be teleportation or time alteration. Whichever it is, you can get real close to True Magic within your territory.
...I underestimated you, Caster. No, really, no wonder you talk a good game."

page65.text: While looking up at Caster, Archer adjusts the grip on his twin swords.

page66.text:
"Is that so? Yet you are all disappointment, Archer.
I tested you since I thought you might come in handy, but you're less than Assassin if this is the result."

page67.text:
"Your words pain me. I can do better if you'd grace me with another chance."
"...Of course not. Fools do not get second chances.
Disappear now, Archer."

page68.text:
"Shi—!"
Archer becomes a streak.
He takes off at full speed to get clear from Caster and this place.

page69.text:
"Heh, you think you can get away...!?"
Caster's staff moves.
The moment it points at Archer...
Something absurd flashes before my very eyes.

page70.text:
"N—"
No one can hear me say "No way!"

page71.text:
Caster's attack is like a deluge of rain.
The light that streaks down is like a bombing raid.
Each spell is a deathblow, and Caster rains them down uninhibited.
I may be green at this, but even I can tell how off the charts this magecraft is.

page72.text:
This is more like a grand magecraft.
Something like that requires a magic circle and a ten count instant contract...an incantation of at least ten lines.
Because grand magecraft is powerful, it requires more time to cast it.
A normal mage would take a minute to cast such magecraft.
Even a mage that uses high-speed incantation would take thirty seconds.

page73.text:
But she did it in an instant.
She didn't even need an incantation and just pointed her staff. And she's using it continuously; I can't even think of anyone who would compare...!

page74.text: "Ugh...! You damn fox. You must have stored an incredible amount of magical energy to be able to fire A-rank magecraft in succession like this!"

page75.text:
He must've decided that he can't avoid them all anymore, as Archer sprints while deflecting them with his twin swords.
Archer makes for the exit, but changes course halfway there as if he just remembered something.

page76.text:
"You fool...!
How long are you just going to stand there!?"
Archer charges towards me with a fierce look.

page77.text:
"Huh?"
That makes me realize.
The place I'm standing is no longer safe.
I'm already in the range of the rain of light...!

page78.text:
"Damn it, why am I stuck doing this!?"
Archer makes toward me.
"Guh...!"
The moment I try to jump back to avoid him...

page79.text: My body is flying through the air.

page80.text:
"Huh?"
I try to shake him off reflexively.
...You've got to be shitting me.
Archer's now carrying me!?

page81.text:
"Ugh...! Let me down, you idiot! What the hell are you thinking!?"
"How would I know! Shut up, hearing that from you is giving me a headache from how stupid I'm being, idiot!"

page82.text:
"Idiot!? You call me an idiot knowing you're an idiot yourself!? You idiot!"
"Ugh...! Hey, are you a child or something!? I don't know what you're gonna do if you're stupid and a child! At least pick one, you fool!"

page83.text:
Archer must be wound up, as his words make no sense.
But, even though he saved me, I just can't graciously accept.

page84.text: "You... Just let go of me! I can take care of myself! I don't need your help!"

page85.text:
No, more than that, I can't bear being a hindrance to him.
Archer should've been able to escape by now if it was just himself.
But the exit is farther now that he's saved me.
Archer running around the temple must be an easy target for Caster, who is above us.

page86.text:
"Archer! Are you listening to me...!?"
"...I see. Then I don't need to hold back."
Then...
Archer drop-kicks me.

page87.text:
"Guh...!?"
I tumble onto the ground.
He must've kicked me hard, as I flew at least five meters.

page88.text:
"You..."
I endure the pain and get up.
"...Huh?"
Archer is still.
The rain of light bullets has also stopped.
All that remains is a feeling of cold that hurts my ears.

page89.text:
"...Hey..."
I finally get my bearings.
The very air around Archer has frozen.

page90.text:
"How are you feeling, Archer? Even as one of the three knights, you can't move if space itself is frozen."
Caster's triumphant voice.
Archer must not be able to talk. It's like time has stopped for him.

page91.text:
"I guess this is it. Saber is outside, so I don't have any more time to waste on you.
I don't know which Heroic Spirit you are, but this is goodbye, Archer."

page92.text:
Caster raises her left hand.
From that hand, the light bullet of instant death is dropped.
But, right before that...
Archer murmurs something.

page93.text:
"Hmm? What is it, Archer? If you feel like begging for mercy, I may—"
"...said...Caster..."

page94.text:
His tone is filled with irritation.
I try to make out what he's saying, and—
"...You fool, I said to dodge it, Caster!"
Archer leaps away.

page95.text:
He must've broken the frozen space with force.
With the sound of breaking glass, Archer flashes out of sight.

page96.text:
"W-what are—"
Distracted by Archer's angry shout, Caster is baffled.
And then to either side of her...
A flash of black and white converge on her.

page97.text:
"Guh!!!"
Caster's robe tears.
She must've been given just enough warning from Archer's shout and narrowly escapes the attack.

page98.text: It should not need explaining, but it is Archer's blades that fly by.

page99.text:
It was in an instant.
Archer threw the twin swords to either side when he kicked me and got caught in the freezing spell.
The blades boomeranged through the sky and made an arc back toward Caster.

page100.text:
"Guess you gotta hand it to him... Wait, where did he go...
...Guh...!?"
I'm left speechless.
Caster too.
The red knight leaps back into view and calls checkmate.

page101.text:
He kneels on the ground and aims his bow towards the sky.
His target is Caster.
And the arrow he has nocked is the same magical blade that he shot at Berserker...!

page102.text:
"...I am the bone of my sword."
Archer's voice shakes the air.
"......!"
Caster weaves an urgent incantation.
But having clearly anticipated that...

page105.text:
Is that his Noble Phantasm?
The released arrow twists space itself.

page106.text:
"Haah...!"
Caster's moan fills the air.
The tornado-like arrow easily penetrated Caster's defense.

page107.text: Most likely... Guessing from the distortion, I bet Caster would've been twisted along with space itself even if she had teleported.

page108.text:
"Ah... Ah..."
...Even then, Caster's still alive.
The black robe has scattered, and the body underneath the robe has numerous cuts.
Caster is using all her magical energy to regenerate, but I'm sure she would've died instantly without a chance to heal had it been a direct hit.

page109.text:
...Yeah.
Archer's shot did not land a direct hit.
The arrow was released into an empty space away from Caster, and her barrier of protection was destroyed from the aftermath.

page110.text:
The arrow missed.
...No, that's wrong.
He did not miss. He deliberately did not hit her.
I don't know what his intentions are.
Though he had the chance to finish her off, for whatever reason, Archer let her go.

page111.text:
...Stillness returns to the temple.
Archer remains in front of me, while Caster floats down, glaring at Archer all the while.
That last attack must've taken a lot out of him, as I can sense that Archer's magical energy is low.

page112.text:
That goes for Caster as well.
Although it missed, Archer's attack scraped away most of Caster's body and magical energy.
Even if there was a big pool of magical energy here, it's useless if Caster is too injured to collect.

page113.text:
"Khh... Ah..."
Caster lands, dispirited.
She seems to have managed to reform her body, but she's running on empty inside.
It should be impossible to continue fighting.

page114.text:
"Hnng... Ungh... Khh...!"
Caster stares at us while breathing heavily.
For some reason, she seems to be comparing the both of us.

page115.text:
"...Archer. Why didn't you hit me with that shot?"
The demoralization is in her voice as well.
Archer shrugs as if to say it should be obvious.

page116.text:
"Well, I said that I would only try once.
My first attack didn't work. Everything else didn't really matter. What? Did you want me to break our promise and hit you instead?"
He's crazy.

page117.text:
"...So you had no intention of killing me?"
"I just responded to your provocation. My objective was that guy over there. I didn't actually intend to start a fight, here."

page118.text:
...Hm.
He really didn't seem to come here with any hostility at first.

page119.text:
"...I see. So you really did not come spoiling for a fight."
"Yeah, I'm the same as that coward over there. It's my policy to avoid meaningless battles.
I prefer to wield my sword at opportune moments, and most preferably when I can ensure a kill. Meaningless bloodshed isn't my thing."

page120.text:
...I don't know what's so funny.
But Caster gives a hearty laugh.

page121.text:
"I see. So you two are similar then?"
"What?"
We reply in unison.
Similar... Me and that guy?
What makes her say that?

page122.text:
"Am I wrong? You both do not like pointless killing, right? That boy over there cannot forgive Servants who feed on innocent humans like me.
You do not like meaningless slaughter.
See, it is exactly the same. Is that not why you two are cooperating?"

page123.text: "Stupi—How do you figure that!? Get your eyes checked! How the hell could anyone think we're even remotely alike!?"

page124.text:
"...I feel the same way. We may both prefer pacifism, but our principles are vastly different. My policy is to get rid of nuisances early on.
I'm not a ponderous oaf like this guy."

page125.text:
"Khh...! Pacifist my ass! I haven't forgotten. You shot at Saber along with Berserker.
You made Saber fight by herself while you hid safely far away!"

page126.text:
"It is what it is. We didn't have a truce then. Berserker's defeat was a far greater priority than Saber's safety.
Or what? Don't tell me that you're telling me to save everything that I see. In that case, Berserker wouldn't be someone that you have to defeat, either."
"Agh...!"

page127.text:
We glare at each other.
Man, I really don't get along with this guy!
Why does everything he says get on my nerves...!?

page128.text:
"Heh..."
Meanwhile...
Caster's laugh is even more amused as she looks between us.

page129.text:
"I like you two. Both your strength and the way you both are is a scarcity.
It would be disappointing to make you two my enemies."
"Hm?"
My head tilts in confusion.
Archer looks away from me and glares at Caster.

page130.text:
"...Hold on. What are you saying?"
"Is it not obvious? I'm saying you should work with me.
I can offer you both something better than your current partners.
You, boy, I can give a Servant greater than Saber.
And you, Archer, I can grant a contract with a mage superior to yours."

page131.text:
My mind grinds to a halt.
I question her sanity and seriousness.

page132.text:
"I should think it a tempting proposal. I have what it takes to end this war. I told you that it is easy for me to win.
What do you think? If survival is the goal, it is a promising offer, no?"

page133.text:
"..."
There's not even an option here.
I decided to fight to stop those who involve innocent people.
As such, I can't accept the offer of someone like her.

page134.text:
"...I refuse. I can't cooperate with a witch like you."
That's all there is to it.
It should be obvious where I'd stand.
I can't ally myself with this Servant, nor can I betray those I'm already partnered with.
I'm going to fight alongside Saber and Archer would also never betray Tohsaka.

page136.text:
"...Hey. Archer, you...!"
"...I refuse. I don't have a reason to take the power you offer.
To start with, your territory is too weak. No matter how much stronger you make it, it will never be as strong as Berserker. The conditions aren't good enough to accept."

page137.text:
...
...I sigh with relief.
I had a bad feeling, but he's not like that.
I hate him, but he's firm on his beliefs.

page138.text:
"I see. So negotiations have failed, hmm?"
"That is right. But I have no intention of fighting you here. It is by my own choice that I am here. It is not my Master's order, so I have no reason to cut you down. How about we call this a draw?"

page139.text:
"Huh...?"
I doubt my own ears.
Did he just say that he's going to let Caster go...?

page140.text:
"...That is surprising. Your Master was after me, right? Yet, you are going to let me go?"
"Yeah. I don't care how many people you kill here. That does not concern me."

page141.text:
"...Oh my. What a terrible man. You think poison has its uses?"
"My Master is not so enthusiastic about killing other Masters.
So it will help me if you can do so. We can settle our match after that."

page143.text:
Caster seems to have accepted Archer's proposal, as she turns around.
I run to Caster as she moves to vanish.
But Archer stops me.

page144.text:
"Are you stupid? You're gonna get yourself killed that way."
He says indifferently.
Though true, his words make me feel so furious I make myself nauseous.

page145.text:
"Ugh..."
I stop.
Caster's black gown flutters in the wind and disappears like magic.
